en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Dukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (2) 14.23.
Cetasikaduka, etc.

Dependent on a mental state (*cetasika*), a non-mental state arises by way of root condition (*hetu-paccaya*). [Under] root [condition] there are nine; ... pe ... under prenascence and repetition conditions there are five; ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are nine.
Dependent on a state associated with consciousness (*cittasampayutta*), a state not associated with consciousness arises by way of root condition;
... pe .... Dependent on a state conjoined with consciousness (*cittasaṃsaṭṭha*), a state not conjoined with consciousness arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root condition, nine; in the case of object condition, three; in the case of predominance condition, five … pe … in the case of mutuality condition, six; in the cases of prenascence and repetition conditions, one … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition, nine.

Dependent on a state produced by consciousness, there arises a state not produced by consciousness by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. In the case of root condition, nine; in the case of object condition, nine;
in the case of predominance condition, five … pe … in the cases of prenascence and repetition conditions, five … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition, nine.

Dependent on a state coexistent with consciousness (*cittasahabhū*), a state not coexistent with consciousness arises by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*) …pe… dependent on a state that accompanies consciousness (*cittānuparivatti*),
a state not accompanying consciousness arises by way of the root-condition …pe… dependent on a state conjoined with and produced by consciousness (*cittasaṁsaṭṭhasamuṭṭhāna*),
a state not conjoined with and produced by consciousness arises by way of the root-condition …pe… [dependent on] a state coexistent with what is conjoined with and produced by consciousness …pe…
Dependent on a state that is not conjoined with, produced by, or co-existent with consciousness, a state arises by way of root condition … pe … dependent on a state that is conjoined with,
produced by, and follows upon consciousness, a state that is not conjoined with, produced by,
or follows upon consciousness arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of the root condition, there are nine; ... [and so on] ... in the case of the prenascence and repetition conditions, there are five; ... [and so on] ... in the case of the non-disappearance condition, there are nine.
Dependent on an internal state, a non-internal state arises by way of the root condition; ... three.
Dependent on an external state, a non-external state arises by way of the root condition; ... three.
Dependent on internal and external phenomena, a non-internal phenomenon arises by way of the root condition... three. (Abbreviated. Nine for the root;
five for the object; five for the predominance... pe ... five for the prenascence and repetition conditions... pe ... nine for the non-disappearance.
Dependent on derived phenomena, a non-derived phenomenon arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not derived (*noupādā*), a state that is not derived arises by way of the root condition (*hetupaccaya*)—three [answers].

Dependent on a state that is both derived and not derived, a state that is not derived arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. Under the root condition there are five; under the object condition (*ārammaṇa*), three;

under the predominance condition (*adhipati*), three ... pe ... under the prenascence and repetition conditions (*purejāta*, *āsevana*), one ... pe ... under the non-disappearance condition (*avigata*), five.
Dependent on a state that is clung-to (*upādinna*), a state that is not clung-to arises by way of the root-condition (*hetupaccaya*)—three [cases].
Dependent on a state that is not clung-to, a state that is not non-clung-to arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is both clung-to and not clung-to, a state that is not clung-to arises by way of the root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root condition, five; in the case of object condition, two; in the case of predominance condition, one …pe… in the case of repetition condition, one …pe… in the case of non-disappearance condition, five. (The detailed exposition applies in all cases.
The Great Intermediate Set of Twos is finished.
